## Exact cancellation

Write M_l=sum L_i v_i^(2l), H0=-(2/a)M_0-(tau cap+alpha) C_b. For v above all source indices, combine the entire pole denominator with the sine term:

    -(2/a)sum L_i v/(v^2-v_i^2) -(tau cap+alpha) C_b v/(v^2+1/4)
      = H0 v/(v^2+1/4)
        -(2/a) v/(v^2+1/4) sum L_i(v_i^2+1/4)/(v^2-v_i^2).

The saved signed moments give centered moments M_(l+1)+M_l/4 for l=0..6. Expand the centered denominator for seven terms with the same geometric remainder. Bound the remaining absolute moment by sum 4(|d_i|+|t_i|)(v_i^2+1/4)v_i^14. Here |A_i^P|<4, |A_i^G|<=2(1/v_i+pi/4)<4 for ALL source sine indices since v_i>=15/11 and pi<22/7. Use v_i<=10i/7; |t_i|<=|d_i|+|tau| 33/(15i) on low modes since |C_b|<3 and v_i>=15i/11. High t_i=q_i. For the two remaining sine lists retain the original eight signed moments and bound the final absolute moments using these same upper coefficient bounds and v_i<=10i/7. The old pole column and logarithmic upper charges remain, with H0/v and no separately charged large v^-3 pole term. Count all indices >2048 and use the same decreasing integral/Minkowski bounds. Upward roots on 10^100 grid, exact rational JS BigInt computations.
